messages:
Asha (runtime): Quick sync from the postmortem — we need an action plan that reduces blast radius and gives us observability into fragmentation. root causes: slow KV-residency increase per-shard, allocator fragmentation, and OOMs with certain seq patterns.
Miguel: +1. Propose two tracks: immediate safety guards and telemetry/profiling work.
Priya: Immediate guard: per-shard soft eviction + per-tenant hard cap. I'll own the implementation. ETA: Fri EOD. @Miguel can you add tests and a small harness?
Miguel: On it. I'll add unit tests and a QPS-based integration test replicating residency growth. ETA Wed.
Jin: I'll run allocator-sampling runs and collect heap/prof traces (cold, warm, sustained 10min). Will upload to INF-842.
Asha (runtime): Jin, please include commands and sample pprof exports. Example:
```
pprof -http=localhost:8080 /srv/runtime/proc --alloc_space
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/debug/pprof/heap > heap.pprof
```
Miguel: Also adding a CI check: after 5m of synthetic load, per-shard residency must not exceed 10% growth. Filing ticket for CI job.
Priya: Ownership recap: Priya -> eviction + hard caps + rollback gating; Miguel -> tests, CI job, PR links; Jin -> profiler traces + GC experiments; Sam -> canary and 48h monitoring.
Sam (oncall): I'll run the canary and tune alerts: tighten KV-residency slope alert to detect earlier drift.
Asha (runtime): Timeline: soft fixes + alert tweaks by EOW; canary next Tue; GC/allocator tuning in next sprint (2w). Any blockers?
Miguel: None. I'll ensure PRs reference the postmortem and add changelog notes.
Jin: Telemetry item: add fragmentation metric (resident_chunks / alloc_chunks) and a dashboard. I'll prototype the query and post here.
Priya: Rollback playbook: if canary shows >5% error rate or memory drift >20% sustained over 30m, revert to previous image and open incident.
infra-bot: Runbook snippet and alert thresholds added to ticket INF-842.
Asha (runtime): Check-in Friday 10:00 PT to confirm progress. Marking actions as in-progress in the postmortem. Thanks. :rocket:
